title: Punctuation
examples: When should I use a comma in a list?
What is the difference between a full stop and a comma?
Can I use an apostrophe to show possession?

explain.say: Today we are learning about punctuation marks in writing.

items: Commas separate items in a list.

draw.text: Punctuation Marks: Full Stop, Comma, Question Mark, Exclamation Mark

explain.say: A full stop marks the end of a simple statement.

draw.text: Statement ends with a full stop (.)

explain.say: We use commas to separate things when we list them.
A question mark shows that you are asking something.

draw.text: Question ends with a question mark (?)

explain.say: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling or excitement.

draw.text: Excitement ends with an exclamation mark (!)

explain.say: Apostrophes show ownership or missing letters.

faq.q: When do I use an apostrophe?
faq.a: You use an apostrophe to show that something belongs to someone or something. You also use it when letters are missing in a short word.

faq.q: What is the difference between a full stop and a comma?
faq.a: A full stop stops you completely, like a period. A comma is a short pause, like taking a breath while listing things.
asks: When do I pause my voice?
Is a comma stronger than a full stop?

faq.q: When do I use a question mark?
faq.a: You use a question mark when your sentence is asking something. It shows that the reader should expect an answer.
asks: How do I write a question?
Does a question always start with a capital letter?

faq.q: When should I use an exclamation mark?
faq.a: Use an exclamation mark when you want to show strong feeling, like surprise or excitement. It makes your writing sound loud.
asks: How do I show I am shouting?
Can I use it for everything?

faq.q: Do I need punctuation at the end of every sentence?
faq.a: Yes, almost every complete sentence needs punctuation at the end. This tells the reader when to stop reading.
asks: Is it okay to leave it blank?

facts: A full stop marks the end of a declarative sentence.
Commas are used to separate items in a series or list.
Question marks are used for direct questions.
Apostrophes show possession, like 'the dog's bone'.

quiz.say: Which punctuation mark ends a sentence that asks something?
quiz.why: The question mark is the correct punctuation for any sentence that asks something.

wrong.0: This is wrong because an exclamation mark shows excitement, not a question.
wrong.2: This is wrong because a full stop shows a statement, not a question.
wrong.3: This is wrong because a comma only shows a short pause, not the end of a question.

quiz.say: What punctuation mark shows that the book belongs to Sarah?
quiz.why: The apostrophe is used to show that something belongs to a person or thing.

wrong.1: This is wrong because a full stop ends a sentence, it does not show ownership.
wrong.2: This is wrong because a comma separates things in a list, not ownership.
wrong.3: This is wrong because a question mark is only used when asking a question.

quiz.say: Look at this list: apples, oranges, and bananas. What punctuation is needed?
quiz.show: List punctuation: apples, oranges, and bananas
quiz.why: You need a comma after 'apples' to separate the first two items in the list correctly.

wrong.0: This is wrong because an exclamation mark shows excitement, not just a pause in a list.
wrong.1: This is wrong because an apostrophe shows ownership, not separation in a list.
wrong.3: This is wrong because a full stop ends the sentence, but there are more items to list.
